'''Giorgio Margaritondo''' (born {{birth date|1946|8|24}} in [[Rome]], Italy) is a Swiss and American [[physicist]] and an emeritus professor at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL)]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=ORCID|title=Giorgio Margaritondo (0000-0002-1243-7686)|url=https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1243-7686|access-date=2020-12-08|website=orcid.org|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Giorgio Margaritondo's page at EPFL|url=https://people.epfl.ch/giorgio.margaritondo?lang=en|access-date=8 December 2020|website=EPFL}}</ref> He is known for his pioneering work in the use and dissemination of [[synchrotron radiation]] and [[Free-electron laser|free electron lasers]].

He is currently affiliated to the Laboratory for Quantum Magnestism and leads the laboratory for Science History at EPFL.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Members|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/lqm/members/|access-date=2020-12-08|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Truth in science history|url=https://sciencehistory.epfl.ch/|access-date=2020-12-08|website=sciencehistory.epfl.ch|language=en-US}}</ref>

== Career ==
Margaritondo graduated with a diploma ([[Laurea]]) in physics from the [[University of Rome Unitelma Sapienza|University of Rome]] in 1969. After being employed by the [[National Research Council (Italy)|Italian National Research Council]] in Rome until 1975, he moved to the [[Bell Labs|Bell Laboratories]] in the United States. In 1978, he was appointed Professor at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison|University of Wisconsin-Madison]], where he was named Associate Director for research of the [[Synchrotron Radiation Center]]. In 1990, he was named Full Professor at the [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL)]], where he directed the Institute of Applied Physics and the Physics Department. He was subsequently named [[Dean (education)|Dean]] of EPFL's School of Basic Sciences in 2001, and [[Provost (education)|Provost]] in 2004. In 2010 he became Dean of Continuing Education at EPFL, until he retired in 2016.<ref name=":1" />

He currently serves as the President of the Scientific and Technological Committee of the [[Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia|Italian Institute of Technology]] (IIT).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Giorgio MARGARITONDO – SYNAPSE|url=https://synapse-sg.org/team/prof-giorgio-margaritondo/|access-date=2020-12-17|language=en-US}}</ref>

Margaritondo has authored more than 1000 peer-reviewed scientific publications and is the author of several books.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Giorgio Margaritondo's profile on Google Scholar|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=ISPrF2YAAAAJ&hl=en&oi=ao|access-date=2020-12-17|website=scholar.google.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Books authored by Giorgio Margaritondo|url=https://www.amazon.co.uk/Books-Giorgio-Margaritondo/s?rh=n:266239,p_27:Giorgio+Margaritondo|access-date=2020-12-17|website=www.amazon.co.uk|language=en-gb}}</ref>

== Research ==
Margaritondo has been one of the pioneers in the use of synchrotron radiation and free electron lasers.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Margaritondo, Giorgio, 1946-|title=Introduction to synchrotron radiation|date=1988|publisher=Oxford University Press|isbn=0-19-504524-6|location=New York|oclc=16465449}}</ref> He has developed and applied several of the basic techniques in this domain, including microscopy, spectroscopy (photoemission, stimulated desorption), coherent imaging.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Gallucci|first1=E.|last2=Scrivener|first2=K.|last3=Groso|first3=A.|last4=Stampanoni|first4=M.|last5=Margaritondo|first5=G.|date=2007-03-01|title=3D experimental investigation of the microstructure of cement pastes using synchrotron X-ray microtomography (μCT)|url=http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0008884606002638|journal=Cement and Concrete Research|series=Cementitious Materials as model porous media: Nanostructure and Transport processes|language=en|volume=37|issue=3|pages=360–368|doi=10.1016/j.cemconres.2006.10.012|issn=0008-8846|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Katnani|first1=A. D.|last2=Margaritondo|first2=G.|date=1983-08-15|title=Microscopic study of semiconductor heterojunctions: Photoemission measurement of the valance-band discontinuity and of the potential barriers|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevB.28.1944|journal=Physical Review B|volume=28|issue=4|pages=1944–1956|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.28.1944|bibcode=1983PhRvB..28.1944K |url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=New Technology Reads Ancient Documents without Opening Them|url=https://learningenglish.voanews.com/a/new-technology-reads-ancient-document-withoutv-reading-them/4210686.html|access-date=2020-12-17|website=VOA|language=en}}</ref> He developed original ways to present synchrotron radiation to a broad audience.

== Distinctions ==
Margaritondo was awarded with numerous prizes and rewards, such as the John Yarwood Memorial Medal of the [[British Vacuum Council]] in 1995 and the Romnes Award in 1983.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Giorgio Margaritondo's CV|url=https://www.iit.it/scientific-technical-committee/780-margaritondo-en|access-date=2020-12-08|website=Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia}}{{Dead link|date=December 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>

He is Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] and of the [[American Vacuum Society]] and Fellow and Chartered Physicist of the [[Institute of Physics]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last=|first=|date=2011|title=New Editor-in-Chief for Journal of Physics D: Applied Physics|journal=Journal of Physics D: Applied Physics|volume=44|issue=16|article-number=160301|doi=10.1088/0022-3727/44/16/160301|s2cid=250892977|doi-access=free}}</ref>

He has been an honorary Faculty member at the [[Vanderbilt University]] in [[Nashville, Tennessee|Nashville]].<ref name=":1" />
